title: Unsafe deserialization via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} rebuilds objects from a byte stream without a type allowlist, so the payload itself chooses which classes are constructed. Prefer a data-only format; when a native serializer is required, pass an explicit allowlist ({safe}). This lexical rule flags the call and does not resolve where the bytes come from.
remediation: Replace {sink} with a data-only parser, or constrain the accepted types ({safe}).
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the {sink} call; origin of the bytes and the reachable classes are out of scope.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Integrity-checked internal caches and trusted fixtures are the accepted false positives.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} reconstructs objects from untrusted bytes and lets the payload name the classes that run. A crafted stream can therefore execute code during construction. Use a data-only format, or an explicit allowlist ({safe}), and authenticate the payload before parsing it.
applicability: {lang} services that deserialize stored or networked data; single-line lexical scope.
risk: Code execution when the stream is attacker influenced; HIGH severity.
fix: If unavoidable, restrict the permitted types ({safe}) and verify the payload signature.
verifyT: Rescan shows no {sink} call, and a round-trip test covers the replacement.

title: Multi-document YAML load via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} parses every document in a YAML stream with the default loader, which can construct arbitrary Python objects. Each document multiplies the exposure. Use {safe}. This lexical rule flags the call; whether Loader was set is reviewed separately.
remediation: Use {safe}, or pass the safe loader explicitly for every document.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the {sink} call; a safe Loader argument on the same call is visible but not proven.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: A call that already passes SafeLoader is the common accepted case.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} parses each document of a YAML stream with the default loader. YAML tags can name Python constructors, so a crafted multi-document file can build dangerous objects before any application validation. Use the safe loader for every document ({safe}).
applicability: {lang} configuration and import paths that accept multi-document YAML; lexical scope.
risk: Code execution from a crafted document set; HIGH severity.
why: {sink} parses each YAML document without a safe loader.
fix: Reject unexpected YAML tags before use.
verifyT: Rescan shows no {sink} call and the safe loader is covered by a test.

title: Password-based cipher without an IV via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} derives a key from a passphrase (an OpenSSL EVP_BytesToKey style KDF) and decrypts with a legacy algorithm without an explicit IV. The same passphrase therefore yields the same keystream, and the key stretching is far too cheap. Use an authenticated cipher with {safe} and a managed key.
remediation: Move to an authenticated cipher with an explicit IV ({safe}) and a real KDF such as scrypt or Argon2.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the {sink} call; algorithm strength and key management are reviewed separately.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Decrypting legacy data that was written years ago is a documented exception with a migration plan.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} turns a passphrase into a cipher key and decrypts without an explicit IV. Repeated use of the passphrase repeats the keystream, which leaks plaintext relationships, and the legacy cipher offers no authentication. Use an AEAD cipher with {safe} and a managed key.
applicability: {lang} code that protects stored or transported data; lexical scope only.
risk: Plaintext recovery and undetected tampering; MEDIUM severity.
fix: Rotate any data that was protected under the old scheme.
verifyT: Rescan shows no {sink} call and the new cipher round-trips with a random IV.

title: Predictable identifier via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} generates an identifier from the current time and a small counter, so values are guessable and collide under load. It is not a source of unguessable tokens. For security values use {safe}. This lexical rule flags the call; whether the value guards anything is reviewed separately.
remediation: Use a cryptographic source ({safe}) for tokens and identifiers that must not be guessable.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the {sink} call; the value’s security role is a review question.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: A filename suffix in a local cache is a harmless use.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} builds an identifier from time and a counter rather than from a random source. An attacker who can approximate the time and observe one value can predict neighbours, and concurrent calls can collide. Security tokens need {safe}.
applicability: {lang} code that mints identifiers for tokens, links or sessions; lexical scope.
risk: Predictable identifiers and collisions; LOW severity.
fix: Replace {sink} with a cryptographic random generator ({safe}).
Keep the old format acceptable only for non-security identifiers.
verifyT: Rescan shows no {sink} call on a security path.

title: HTML parsing insertion via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} parses its string argument as markup and inserts the result into the document, so any attacker-influenced character becomes live DOM. When the value is text rather than markup, use {safe}. This lexical rule flags the call; it does not trace the argument.
remediation: Insert untrusted text with {safe}, or sanitize markup with a maintained sanitizer before insertion.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the {sink} call; the argument’s provenance is out of scope.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Inserting a constant template that contains no user data is the accepted case.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} converts a string into nodes instead of text. A value that reaches it from a URL, storage or an API therefore becomes executable markup, including event-handler attributes. Insert text with {safe}, or sanitize markup first.
applicability: {lang} browser code that renders server or user supplied strings; lexical scope.
risk: Script execution in the victim origin; MEDIUM severity.
fix: Use {safe} when the value is plain text.
Sanitize with a maintained library before inserting markup.
verifyT: Rescan shows no {sink} call on a user-influenced path.
